conditions_text: Indian ordinary-passport holders (and accompanying family) who hold a valid US visa or US Green Card (or a UK/EU visa or residence permit, or a residence permit from Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, Singapore or New Zealand) can get a UAE entry visa under the UAE's scheme for Indian nationals. Official pages (ICP and Dubai GDRFA) call it a 'visa on arrival' but the service is applied for and paid online through the GDRFA smart-services portal, takes about 48 hours and is emailed to you, so arrange it before you fly; the visa must be used within 30 days of issue. Two stay options appear on the official pages: 14 days (extendable once for a further 14 days) and 60 days (single entry, not extendable); the pages do not say which one a given applicant is issued, so plan on 14. The passport and the US visa/Green Card must each have at least 6 months' validity. Overstay fine is AED 50 per day. Source note: ICP's 25 June 2026 announcement lists the current eligibility, durations and fees; the GDRFA Indian-citizen service page (older wording) lists only the Green Card and UK/EU residence visa.
fee_notes: ICP (25 June 2026): AED 100 total issuance fee for the 14-day visa (extendable once); AED 250 for the 60-day visa. The GDRFA Indian-citizen page shows a fee of '253' with no currency, and the ICP 60-day service page shows AED 250 plus a AED 100 smart-services fee (AED 350 total), so confirm the amount at the point of payment. Not free.

conditions_text: Indian passport holders need a visa for the UAE; the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the Republic of India as 'Visa Required'. The exception is the scheme for Indian nationals holding a valid US visa or Green Card, a UK/EU visa or residence permit, or a residence permit from Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, Singapore or New Zealand: see the cascade rule for a held US document. Otherwise a visa must be arranged in advance (through an airline, sponsor or the official UAE portals) before travel.

Indian nationals can get Turkey's e-Visa only if they hold a supporting document: a valid visa or residence permit from a Schengen country, the USA, the UK or Ireland (e-visas from other countries are not accepted). The supporting visa must be valid on the date you enter Turkey (used or unused is fine); the originals must be shown at Turkish immigration, and airlines will refuse boarding if the document does not qualify. The e-Visa is single entry, valid for one month, and only for tourism or commerce.
fee_notes: Paid e-visa applied for online at evisa.gov.tr only (the embassy warns non-official sites overcharge). The embassy page gives no amount, only that it costs at least 85 USD less than a sticker visa; check the exact fee on evisa.gov.tr.

conditions_text: Turkey's foreign ministry lists Indian ordinary passport holders as requiring a visa. The e-Visa is available only with a valid US, UK, Irish or Schengen visa or residence permit; without one, a sticker visa must be obtained in advance from a Turkish embassy or consulate.

Indian nationals normally need a Mexican visa (India is on INM's list of countries that require one), but the INM page lists a valid, unexpired visa from the United States as an accepted alternative to a Mexican visa, alongside proof of permanent residence there. With one of these documents you may enter as a tourist or business visitor without a Mexican visa, still with a valid passport. By air there is no paper form: the digital FMM (FMMd) is generated at immigration and the officer stamps your passport with the days granted. By land you must carry a completed FMM (it can be filled in online beforehand or at the border). Visitors may not stay more than 180 days; the officer sets the actual days. No paid work. Confirm with the nearest Mexican consulate that your specific visa qualifies before booking.
fee_notes: The migratory fee for tourist entry is set each year in the Ley Federal de Derechos (2026 rates from 1 January 2026); the peso amount was not confirmed from a readable official page. Check the INM 2026 fee table.

conditions_text: Indian nationals need a Mexican visa for any stay, obtained in advance from a Mexican embassy or consulate (INM lists India among the countries that require a visa; tourism and business need a visitor visa without permission for paid work). Exception: a valid, unexpired visa from the US, Canada, UK, Japan or a Schengen country, or proof of permanent residence in one of those (or Chile, Colombia, Peru), is accepted instead; see the cascade rules. Check with a Mexican consulate that your specific visa or residence document qualifies.

Indian nationals are in Group 3 (consular visa) of Costa Rica's official visa directives (Directrices Generales de Visas, La Gaceta Alcance 148, 17 November 2025, the version in force today), but may enter without a Costa Rican visa if they hold a visa or residence of the United States or Canada that allows multiple entries, in any category (including refugee/asylum status; for visa types D and C1/D only those categories qualify), with at least 1 calendar day of validity counted from the day they enter Costa Rica. US transit visas C1, C2 and C3 are not accepted. The stay granted cannot exceed the validity of that US/Canadian document. The passport must still have at least 180 days of validity, and proof of funds (US$100 per month of stay) and a return or onward ticket are required. The directive also accepts multiple-entry Schengen C/D visas and residence in the UK, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland or an EU country; only the US document is modelled in this app.

Indian nationals are in Group 3 (consular visa) of Costa Rica's official visa directives (Directrices Generales de Visas, La Gaceta Alcance 148, 17 November 2025, the version in force today). Without a qualifying multiple-entry US/Canadian visa or residence (see the held-document rule), a Costa Rican consular visa must be obtained in advance: single entry, to be stamped in the passport within 3 months of approval, then used within 60 business days. The passport must be valid for at least 180 days. Stay is up to 30 days, extendable to a maximum of 90 days.
fee_notes: The consular visa fee is set by Costa Rica's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the directive does not state an amount.

conditions_text: Indian passport holders with a valid US visa or residence permit may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for 90 days in any 180-day period. Georgia's Ordinance No. 256 lists 50 qualifying countries (including the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Ireland, Israel, South Korea, New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Schengen states and several Gulf states); the visa or permit must be valid on the day you cross the border and you must be able to show it. The 2025 amendment that requires Gulf permits to be multiple-entry with at least a year's validity names 17 other nationalities, not India. Without such a visa or permit you need a Georgian e-visa. Since 1 January 2026 every tourist must also carry health and accident insurance covering the whole stay with at least 30,000 GEL of cover (printed or electronic, in English or Georgian; Georgian MFA notice).

Indian passport holders without a qualifying third-country visa or residence permit need a Georgian e-visa (apply online at evisa.gov.ge; there is no visa on arrival). A short-term single-entry visa is issued for up to 30 days; a multiple-entry visa is possible but total stay may not exceed 90 days in any 180. Decisions take at least 5 working days. Passport must be valid 3 months beyond the visa period, have 2 free pages and be issued within the last 10 years. At the border carry a return ticket, proof of accommodation, proof of funds and travel insurance. Since 1 January 2026 every tourist must also carry health and accident insurance covering the whole stay with at least 30,000 GEL of cover (printed or electronic, in English or Georgian; Georgian MFA notice).
fee_notes: Consular fee 20 USD plus a 2% service fee, non-refundable even if refused; the application portal also describes a separate 15 USD identity-verification step (DuVerify).

conditions_text: Indian ordinary-passport holders can get a visa at the Armenian border only if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the EU/Schengen states, the USA, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia or Japan; residence permits from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman also qualify, but only as a physical card or passport sticker. Armenia's page does not state how many days that border visa allows. The passport must be valid for the entire stay. Armenia also has a temporary visa exemption (1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, up to 180 days in a one-year period) for nationals of 111 listed countries who hold a US, EU/Schengen or listed Gulf residence permit valid at least six months from entry; the page does not say whether India is on that list, so do not rely on it without checking the MFA's PDF list.

Indian ordinary-passport holders can apply online at evisa.mfa.am; the Armenian embassy page says processing takes three working days and recommends applying for the e-visa. Applicants need travel medical insurance plus either a valid visa or residence permit from a listed country (EU/Schengen, USA, UK, Canada and others), or an air ticket reservation with return, an invitation from an Armenian host, and proof of financial means. Armenia's page does not state how many days the visa allows. The passport must be valid for the entire stay.

Indian ordinary passports normally need a Serbian visa, but a nationality that needs a visa may enter without one with a valid US visa (or a valid residence permit issued by a US state), for a maximum of 90 days within a six-month period from the day of arrival, provided the documents remain valid for the entire stay. A still-valid visa in an old passport is accepted if the old passport is carried with the new one. If the document expires before the stay ends, apply for a C visa instead. The Serbian embassy in New Delhi's FAQ describes the visa as 'multiple entries'; the welcometoserbia page does not address entries. Different rules apply if you plan to work; longer stays need a D visa.

Ordinary Indian passports require a visa (Serbian MFA: 'Visas required'). Apply for a short-stay C visa (up to 90 days within 180 days from first entry; one, two or more entries) via the online form on welcometoserbia.gov.rs or in person at a Serbian embassy or consulate, no earlier than three months before travel. Serbia offers an e-Visa C only to 'nationals of certain countries'; the official pages do not confirm India is on that list, so do not assume e-visa eligibility. Holders of a valid US, UK, Schengen or EU visa or residence permit can skip this: see the cascade rows.
fee_notes: Visa C consular fee 92 EUR (9,240 INR), 47 EUR for children under 12, per the Serbian embassy in New Delhi price list; the welcometoserbia help page states 90 EUR. Fees move, so confirm before paying.

conditions_text: Since 8 June 2025, Indian nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible, non-convertible 14 days, per the Philippine Embassy (DFA) visa-free page. A passport valid at least 6 months beyond the contemplated stay and a return or onward ticket are required. Other DFA embassy notices (seen in search snippets, not opened) also list a confirmed hotel booking and proof of financial capacity, and some limit the 14 days to tourism while others say tourism or business. Holders of a valid US, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore or UK visa or residence permit get 30 days instead (see the cascade row). Pre-arrival eTravel registration (etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app, free, within 72 hours before arrival, per the official eTravel FAQ and UK FCDO) is required for all arriving foreign passengers; airlines may ask for the QR code at check-in.

Since 8 June 2025, Indian nationals holding a valid, current US visa or residence permit (the DFA's AJACSSUK group: American, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore, UK) may enter the Philippines visa-free for a non-extendible 30 days instead of 14, per the Philippine Embassy (DFA) visa-free page. A passport valid at least 6 months beyond the contemplated stay and a return or onward ticket are required. Pre-arrival eTravel registration (etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app, free, within 72 hours before arrival, per the official eTravel FAQ and UK FCDO) is required for all arriving foreign passengers; airlines may ask for the QR code at check-in.

Indian nationals are on Colombia's conditional visa-exemption list (Resolucion 5488 of 2022, Article 3 Literal C, as amended by Resolucion 3717 of 2023). They may enter without a Colombian visa only if, on arrival, they hold a valid US or Schengen-state residence permit, or a US or Schengen visa valid for at least 180 days at the time of entry. The stay is a short-stay tourism permit of up to 90 days; the immigration officer sets the period on arrival. This row covers the US visa/residence case. A Schengen visa or residence permit works the same way but cannot be modelled as a held document here, so it is described in the no-US-document row. A direct airport-transit stop (up to 24 hours) still needs a transit visa for Indian nationals (Article 8).

Indian nationals who do not meet the conditional exemption (no valid US or Schengen residence permit, and no US or Schengen visa with at least 180 days' validity on arrival) must obtain a Colombian visa before travel from a Colombian consulate (Resolucion 5488 of 2022, Article 7). If you hold a valid Schengen visa (180+ days remaining on arrival) or a Schengen-state residence permit, Article 3 Literal C lets you enter without a Colombian visa instead; the same applies to a US visa or residence permit (see the US-visa row).

Indian ordinary-passport holders can enter Peru without a tourist visa if they hold a visa valid for at least six months from the USA, Canada, the UK, Australia or a Schengen state, or permanent residence in one of those (this row applies if your qualifying document is from the USA; the other qualifying countries have their own rows or are named here). The stay is up to 180 days within 365 days counted from first entry and is not extendable (Supreme Decree 006-2017-RE, in the Foreign Ministry's table of visa requirements). Check at the airline desk that your visa or residence document qualifies.

Indian ordinary-passport holders without a qualifying document (a visa valid at least six months from the USA, Canada, the UK, Australia or a Schengen state, or permanent residence in one of those) must obtain a Peruvian visa in advance from a Peruvian embassy or consulate (the Foreign Ministry table marks India 'Si/No': exempt only under that condition).

India passport holders are on the Indonesian immigration list of nationalities eligible for the single-entry Visitor Visa (visa on arrival, B1): obtain it at the airport on arrival, or apply online in advance as an e-VOA at evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Allows 30 days in Indonesia for tourism, family visits, business meetings or transit, and can be extended once for 30 days (60 days maximum) within Indonesia. Passport valid at least 6 months from arrival; proof of onward or return travel is required. Separately from the visa, the free All Indonesia arrival card (customs and health declaration, allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id) is completed online up to 3 days before arrival and its QR code is shown on arrival (Global Affairs Canada calls it mandatory). Tourists entering Bali also owe the Love Bali tourist levy of IDR 150,000, paid online or on arrival.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 as listed on the official e-visa portal (card payments may carry extra bank fees); the extension is a separate fee. A rise to IDR 750,000 (e-VOA) and IDR 1,000,000 (on arrival) was proposed in August 2026 but, per press reports, has no effective date yet.

conditions_text: Tourist visa is issued on arrival with no pre-approval. Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation (visitmaldives.com, the official Maldives tourism board) states the Maldives 'provides a 30 day free on-arrival visa for all travellers (from any country)' with a booking at a registered Maldivian tourist establishment. Maldives Immigration's own tourist-visa page says only that the tourist visa is granted on arrival and does not state a number of days. That 30-day length applies to all nationalities, and no India-specific 90-day tourist arrangement appears on any Maldivian official page that could be read. India's Ministry of External Affairs, however, lists Maldives in its visa-free table at 90 days, so the two governments' pages differ: plan for 30 days at the border and treat anything longer as an in-country extension (other governments' advice says up to 90 days in total, applied for before the 30 days end). To enter you must show a complete itinerary (confirmed return ticket, prepaid accommodation booking, sufficient funds), a passport with at least 1 month validity (some governments advise 6 months; airlines may apply their own rule), and submit the free IMUGA Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before arrival. The immigration officer decides admissibility at the port.
fee_notes: Visa on arrival and the IMUGA declaration are free; the official site warns some websites charge for the declaration.

conditions_text: Sri Lanka requires every foreign visitor to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online at eta.gov.lk before arrival; this is not visa-free entry. Since 25 May 2026 India is one of 40 nationalities eligible for a free tourist ETA, valid 30 days with double entry permitted within those 30 days from first arrival. Staying longer needs a visa extension, applied for with the Department of Immigration and Emigration and subject to the applicable fee.
fee_notes: Free for the 40 listed nationalities from 25 May 2026 (ETA fees paid before that date are non-refundable). Extension beyond 30 days: applicable visa fee, amount not stated on the page.

conditions_text: The Armenia National Tourism Board's Flights & Visa page says the United States of America (with CIS, EU and Schengen states and a few others) is exempt from an entry visa, that foreigners must show a valid passport, and that visitors from a visa-free country can stay up to 180 days per year. Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs pages (mfa.am) could not be opened, so the exact wording of its unilateral list was not checked. The temporary 2026-27 exemption for residence-permit holders is separate and does not apply to US citizens as such.

No visa needed for tourism: Colombia's Resolucion 5488 of 2022 (Article 3, Literal A) lists Estados Unidos de America among nationalities exempt from the short-stay visa requirement. Tourism permits are for up to 90 days. A one-time extension through Migracion Colombia (Resolucion 2061 of 2020) is possible, up to a total of 180 days in the same calendar year, continuous or discontinuous; it must be requested five business days before the permit expires and is discretionary.

The United States is in Group 1 (no visa) of Costa Rica's official visa directives (Directrices Generales de Visas, La Gaceta Alcance 148, 17 November 2025, the version in force today). The immigration officer on arrival sets the stay, up to 180 calendar days, not extendable (a grant of under 90 days can be extended to a maximum of 90). The passport must be valid for at least one day and the stay granted cannot exceed the passport's validity. Standard entry requirements also apply: proof of funds of at least US$100 per month of stay and a return or onward ticket.

US citizens are on Georgia's list of countries whose citizens may enter and stay without a visa for 1 (one) full year. Border officers can still refuse entry. Since 1 January 2026 every tourist must also carry health and accident insurance covering the whole stay with at least 30,000 GEL of cover (printed or electronic, in English or Georgian; Georgian MFA notice).

USA passport holders are on the Indonesian immigration list of nationalities eligible for the single-entry Visitor Visa (visa on arrival, B1): obtain it at the airport on arrival, or apply online in advance as an e-VOA at evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Allows 30 days in Indonesia for tourism, family visits, business meetings or transit, and can be extended once for 30 days (60 days maximum) within Indonesia. Passport valid at least 6 months from arrival; proof of onward or return travel is required. Tourists entering Bali also owe the Love Bali tourist levy of IDR 150,000, paid online or on arrival.

conditions_text: Tourist visa is issued on arrival with no pre-approval. Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation (visitmaldives.com, the official Maldives tourism board) states the Maldives 'provides a 30 day free on-arrival visa for all travellers (from any country)' with a booking at a registered Maldivian tourist establishment. Maldives Immigration's own tourist-visa page says only that the tourist visa is granted on arrival and does not state a number of days. Stays can be extended, up to 90 days in total, by applying before the 30 days end (per UK, German and Canadian government advice). You must show a complete itinerary (confirmed return ticket, prepaid booking, sufficient funds), a passport with at least 1 month validity per Maldives immigration (some governments advise 6 months), and submit the free IMUGA Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before arrival. The officer decides admissibility at the port.
fee_notes: Free; the IMUGA declaration is also free.

conditions_text: US citizens do not need a visa for tourism, business or transit (the USA is on INM's list of countries that do not require one). Visitors may not stay more than 180 days; the immigration officer decides the days granted and stamps the passport. No paid work. By air there is no paper form: the digital FMM (FMMd) is generated at immigration and the officer stamps your passport with the days granted. By land you must carry a completed FMM (it can be filled in online beforehand or at the border). A valid passport is required.
fee_notes: The migratory fee for tourist entry is set each year in the Ley Federal de Derechos (2026 rates from 1 January 2026); the peso amount was not confirmed from a readable official page. Check the INM 2026 fee table.

conditions_text: No visa is needed for tourism. Peru's Foreign Ministry lists the stay as 90 days, extendable once for an equal period within a 365-day period from first entry; the border officer decides the days granted. Passport should be valid six months beyond arrival; officials may ask for proof of onward travel.

US nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for tourism or business for up to 30 days (Executive Order 408 list), provided they hold a return or onward ticket to their port of origin or next destination and are not subject to a deportation or blacklist order. The DFA list marks US nationals as admissible even with under 6 months' passport validity, but the Philippine Consulate in New York states the standard requirement as 6 months beyond the stay; carry 6 months to avoid being refused boarding. Longer stays need an extension from the Bureau of Immigration after arrival. Pre-arrival eTravel registration (etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app, free, within 72 hours before arrival, per the official eTravel FAQ and UK FCDO) is required for all arriving foreign passengers; airlines may ask for the QR code at check-in.
No visa required for ordinary passports for visits of up to 90 days in a 6-month period starting from the date of first entry (Serbian Ministry of Foreign Affairs).

Sri Lanka requires every foreign visitor to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online at eta.gov.lk before arrival; this is not visa-free entry. Since 25 May 2026 the United States is one of 40 nationalities eligible for a free tourist ETA, valid 30 days with double entry permitted within those 30 days from first arrival. Staying longer needs a visa extension, applied for with the Department of Immigration and Emigration and subject to the applicable fee.
fee_notes: Free for the 40 listed nationalities from 25 May 2026 (ETA fees paid before that date are non-refundable). Extension beyond 30 days: applicable visa fee, amount not stated on the page.

conditions_text: Ordinary passport holders are exempt from a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, per Turkey's foreign ministry. Official passport holders need a visa. Work, study and other long-stay purposes need the relevant visa or permit.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the United States as 'Visa Free'. Per the UAE Embassy in Washington, no advance visa is needed (regular passports only): a visa is issued on entry for a maximum stay of 90 days, continuous or in parts, within 180 days calculated from the date of first entry; this 90 days is non-renewable. The passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond expected arrival, and a round-trip ticket or confirmed ticket to another destination is required. Overstaying incurs a fine of AED 50 per day. (The US State Department page blocked automated fetches, so the UAE Embassy page was used.)
fee_notes: The UAE Embassy page does not state a fee for the entry visa (UK and Canadian government advice describe the equivalent arrival visa as free of charge).

conditions_text: British citizens can visit Armenia without a visa for up to 180 days in a year for tourism or business (UK FCDO travel advice; Armenia's own MFA pages could not be fetched, so this is the UK government's fallback). To stay longer, apply to OVIR (the passports and visas department) in Yerevan. The passport must be valid for the duration of the stay.

British citizens can visit Colombia for up to 90 days for business or tourism without a visa, at the discretion of the immigration officer on arrival (also listed in Resolucion 5488 of 2022, Article 3 Literal A, as Reino Unido). You must be able to show an onward or return ticket valid within the 90-day period. Your passport must be valid on entry, and the Colombian authorities recommend at least 6 months' validity after you plan to leave. Check-Mig online pre-registration (72 hours to 1 hour before travel) is optional per FCDO but speeds up entry. FCDO: you may be able to extend by up to 120 days in Colombia, but cannot stay more than 180 days in any 12 months.

The United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland) is in Group 1 (no visa) of Costa Rica's official visa directives (Directrices Generales de Visas, La Gaceta Alcance 148, 17 November 2025, the version in force today). The immigration officer on arrival sets the stay, up to 180 calendar days, not extendable (a grant of under 90 days can be extended to a maximum of 90). The passport must be valid for at least one day and the stay granted cannot exceed the passport's validity. Standard entry requirements also apply: proof of funds of at least US$100 per month of stay and a return or onward ticket. The UK Foreign Office page also states that British citizens can visit without a visa for up to 180 days at the officer's discretion.

British citizens can visit Georgia without a visa for up to one year (FCDO). Passport should be valid for the duration of the stay. Longer stays, work or study need a longer-term visa or permit. Since 1 March 2026 foreign nationals working in Georgia, including remotely, need a work permit (FCDO). Since 1 January 2026 every tourist must also carry health and accident insurance covering the whole stay with at least 30,000 GEL of cover (printed or electronic, in English or Georgian; Georgian MFA notice).

conditions_text: UK FCDO: you will get a 30-day visa on arrival if you enter as a tourist. You must complete the IMUGA traveller declaration within 96 hours before your flight arrives, and your passport must have an expiry date at least one month after arrival. Maldives immigration also requires a complete itinerary (confirmed return ticket, prepaid booking, sufficient funds). Extension beyond 30 days (up to 90 in total per other governments' advice) is applied for in the Maldives.
fee_notes: Free; the IMUGA declaration is also free.

conditions_text: British citizens do not need a visa for tourism (the UK is on INM's list of countries that do not require one). You receive a passport stamp showing how many days you may stay; up to 180 days, the longest you can stay as a tourist per the UK FCDO. Passport must be valid for the whole stay. By land you must fill in an immigration form online via the INM site; by air some airports have e-gates and you can download digital proof of entry from the INM portal within 60 days (FCDO). No paid work.
fee_notes: No visa fee. FCDO lists other possible costs: a Quintana Roo entry tax payable online, and a departure tax that varies. The migratory fee amount was not confirmed from a readable official page.

conditions_text: No visa is needed for tourism. Peru's Foreign Ministry lists the stay as 90 days, extendable once for an equal period within 365 days from first entry (Migraciones states tourists can receive up to 183 days in total, and FCDO says no more than 183 days in 365). The border officer sets the days granted; airports record entry electronically (TAM Virtual) rather than stamping. Passport must have at least 6 months' validity on arrival.

Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond the contemplated stay. Longer stays need an extension from the Bureau of Immigration after arrival. Pre-arrival eTravel registration (etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app, free, within 72 hours before arrival, per the official eTravel FAQ and UK FCDO) is required for all arriving foreign passengers; airlines may ask for the QR code at check-in. FCDO also states you need an eTravel QR code and proof of onward travel.
No visa required for ordinary passports for visits of up to 90 days in a 6-month period starting from the date of first entry (Serbian Ministry of Foreign Affairs).

fee_notes: Free for the 40 listed nationalities from 25 May 2026 (ETA fees paid before that date are non-refundable). Extension beyond 30 days: applicable visa fee, amount not stated on the page.

conditions_text: Holders of a full British citizen passport can visit visa-free for tourism or business for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must expire at least 150 days after arrival and have at least one blank page. Other types of British passport, and education, work, medical or other special purposes, need a visa.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the United Kingdom as 'Visa Free'. UK FCDO: 'You can get a visitor or tourist visa issued free of charge when you arrive in the UAE', valid for up to 90 days over a 180-day period beginning at first entry, continuous or split across visits. No advance application. Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after arrival (3 months if you hold a UAE residence permit). Working on a visit visa is not permitted. Overstaying can bring fines that accumulate daily. Extensions go through the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai or the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security elsewhere.
fee_notes: Free of charge on arrival (FCDO).

conditions_text: Canadians need a visa to enter Armenia: Canada is not on the Armenian MFA's list of countries whose nationals are unilaterally exempt from the visa requirement (mfa.am/en/visafreelist, 45 states including the US, UK and Australia, not Canada), so the visa-free '180 days per year' allowance does not apply to Canadian citizens. Global Affairs Canada (page updated 27 May 2026) lists tourist, transit and business visas as required, to be obtained before departure through the MFA e-visa site (evisa.mfa.am) or the nearest Armenian embassy. The MFA visa page says 'Armenian visas are issued for a maximum of 120 days with the possibility to extend for another 60 days'; the MFA fee schedule offers visitor visas for up to 21 days and up to 120 days, so the stay depends on the visa category chosen and 120 days is the longest single visitor visa. The e-visa site's own page does not state per-category stay lengths, so confirm the length on the e-visa application. Canada appears only on Armenia's temporary residence-permit exemption list (1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, up to 180 days within one year), which is for holders of a US, EU/Schengen or listed Gulf residence permit, not for Canadians without one. Passport valid at least 6 months beyond planned departure (Global Affairs Canada).
fee_notes: Armenian MFA consular fee schedule (mfa.am/en/fees, valid from 1 January 2026): visitor visa up to 21 days AMD 3,000 (about USD 8); up to 120 days AMD 15,000 (about USD 39); multiple-entry visitor visa up to 120 days with one year validity AMD 40,000 (about USD 103). The schedule does not list e-visa fees separately.

conditions_text: No visa needed for tourist stays of up to 90 days (Global Affairs Canada; Canada is also listed in Resolucion 5488 of 2022, Article 3 Literal A). The immigration officer sets the permitted stay on arrival and overstaying the stamp can bring a fine. Your passport must be valid for the whole stay. Customs may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of funds. Global Affairs Canada says you must complete the free Check-Mig form between 72 hours and 1 hour before travel. You can apply to extend at a Colombian migration office, up to 180 days total per calendar year, at immigration's discretion.

Canada is in Group 1 (no visa) of Costa Rica's official visa directives (Directrices Generales de Visas, La Gaceta Alcance 148, 17 November 2025, the version in force today). The immigration officer on arrival sets the stay, up to 180 calendar days, not extendable (a grant of under 90 days can be extended to a maximum of 90). The passport must be valid for at least one day and the stay granted cannot exceed the passport's validity. Standard entry requirements also apply: proof of funds of at least US$100 per month of stay and a return or onward ticket.

Canadians do not need a tourist visa for stays of up to 365 days (Global Affairs Canada). Passport must be valid for the whole stay and have one blank page for the entry stamp; airlines may apply stricter validity rules. Longer stays need a visa or residence permit obtained in advance. Since 1 January 2026 every tourist must also carry health and accident insurance covering the whole stay with at least 30,000 GEL of cover (printed or electronic, in English or Georgian; Georgian MFA notice).

Canada passport holders are on the Indonesian immigration list of nationalities eligible for the single-entry Visitor Visa (visa on arrival, B1): obtain it at the airport on arrival, or apply online in advance as an e-VOA at evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Allows 30 days in Indonesia for tourism, family visits, business meetings or transit, and can be extended once for 30 days (60 days maximum) within Indonesia. Passport valid at least 6 months from arrival; proof of onward or return travel is required. Separately from the visa, the free All Indonesia arrival card (customs and health declaration, allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id) is completed online up to 3 days before arrival and its QR code is shown on arrival (Global Affairs Canada calls it mandatory). Tourists entering Bali also owe the Love Bali tourist levy of IDR 150,000, paid online or on arrival.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 as listed on the official e-visa portal (card payments may carry extra bank fees); the extension is a separate fee. A rise to IDR 750,000 (e-VOA) and IDR 1,000,000 (on arrival) was proposed in August 2026 but, per press reports, has no effective date yet.

conditions_text: Global Affairs Canada: a 30-day tourist visa can be obtained on arrival and extended for a total stay of no more than 90 days. To get it you must show an onward or return ticket and proof of sufficient funds. Canada's page says passport validity of 6 months from entry; Maldives immigration states 1 month, so carry 6 months to be safe. Maldives immigration also requires the IMUGA Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before arrival (Canada's page does not mention it). Proof of yellow fever vaccination is required if arriving from or transiting a country where yellow fever occurs.
fee_notes: Visa on arrival is free. Canada's page notes a US$50 departure tax payable before boarding an international flight, usually included in the airfare.

conditions_text: Canadians do not need a visa for tourism, for stays up to 180 days; the immigration officer sets the exact days and you cannot extend from inside Mexico. Passport must be valid for the expected duration of the stay (airlines may be stricter). By air you complete a Multiple Digital Migratory Form (FMMD) online on arrival; by land you must complete an FMM (online beforehand, printed, or at the border; not needed for under 72 hours within the northern border zone). A work visa is required for work.
fee_notes: Migratory fee is normally included in airline and cruise tickets. Land arrivals for tourism staying 7 days or less pay nothing; otherwise pay at the entry booth, at a bank afterwards, or online. Peso amount not confirmed (set yearly in the Ley Federal de Derechos).

conditions_text: No visa is needed for tourism. Peru's Foreign Ministry lists the stay as 90 days, extendable once for an equal period within a 365-day period from first entry; Global Affairs Canada states no visa for under 90 days per 365-day period. Passport must be valid at least 6 months after arrival; officials may ask for a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and funds.

Canadian nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for tourism or business for up to 30 days (Executive Order 408 list), provided they hold a return or onward ticket to their port of origin or next destination and are not subject to a deportation or blacklist order. The DFA list marks Canadian nationals as admissible even with under 6 months' passport validity, but Global Affairs Canada says passports must be valid 6 months beyond your departure; carry 6 months to avoid being refused boarding. Longer stays need an extension from the Bureau of Immigration after arrival. Pre-arrival eTravel registration (etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app, free, within 72 hours before arrival, per the official eTravel FAQ and UK FCDO) is required for all arriving foreign passengers; airlines may ask for the QR code at check-in. Global Affairs Canada notes that foreign nationals staying more than 59 days must also register in person at a Bureau of Immigration office.
No visa required for ordinary passports for visits of up to 90 days in a 6-month period starting from the date of first entry (Serbian Ministry of Foreign Affairs).

Sri Lanka requires every foreign visitor to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online at eta.gov.lk before arrival; this is not visa-free entry. Since 25 May 2026 Canada is one of 40 nationalities eligible for a free tourist ETA, valid 30 days with double entry permitted within those 30 days from first arrival. Staying longer needs a visa extension, applied for with the Department of Immigration and Emigration and subject to the applicable fee.
fee_notes: Free for the 40 listed nationalities from 25 May 2026 (ETA fees paid before that date are non-refundable). Extension beyond 30 days: applicable visa fee, amount not stated on the page.

conditions_text: No visa needed for tourist stays of up to 90 days within any 180-day period (confirmed by Turkey's foreign ministry for ordinary passports). Global Affairs Canada says the regular passport must be valid at least 150 days from entry, and that another visa-exempt stay requires leaving Turkey for at least 90 days before re-entering. Work, business, student or medical stays need a visa.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists Canada as 'Visa Free'. Global Affairs Canada (used because UAE embassy pages for Canada could not be opened) says Canadians 'must get a visa on arrival at the port of entry'; it is free and allows a stay of 90 days within a 180-day period. The passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the date of entry, and emergency or temporary passports are not accepted. Some older UAE embassy pages still show shorter figures; the 90-day figure is the one on the Government of Canada page opened today.
fee_notes: Free (Global Affairs Canada).

conditions_text: Smartraveller (updated 17 June 2026) says Australians do not need a visa for Armenia if staying up to 180 days per year; stays beyond 180 days per year need a resident card from Armenia's Migration and Citizenship Service, which can take up to 30 days to process. It says entry conditions can change at short notice and to contact an Armenian embassy or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Armenia's own MFA pages could not be opened. Smartraveller's general 6-month passport note is not an Armenian rule.

conditions_text: Tourist visa is issued on arrival with no pre-approval. Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation (visitmaldives.com, the official Maldives tourism board) states the Maldives 'provides a 30 day free on-arrival visa for all travellers (from any country)' with a booking at a registered Maldivian tourist establishment. Maldives Immigration's own tourist-visa page says only that the tourist visa is granted on arrival and does not state a number of days. Extension up to 90 days in total is applied for in the Maldives (per UK, German and Canadian government advice). You must show a complete itinerary (confirmed return ticket, prepaid booking, sufficient funds), a passport with at least 1 month validity per Maldives immigration (some governments advise 6 months), and submit the free IMUGA Traveller Declaration within 96 hours before arrival. The officer decides admissibility at the port.
fee_notes: Free; the IMUGA declaration is also free.

conditions_text: Australians do not need a pre-arranged visa for tourist trips of 180 days or less (Australia is on INM's list of countries that do not require one). With a chipped ordinary passport you can use e-gates at major airports; you get a printed QR code showing the days authorised. Otherwise you are stamped in for the planned stay. The stamp may give fewer than 180 days and the stay cannot be extended if you stay longer than you told the officer. Smartraveller advises completing an online FMM and keeping the QR code. No paid work.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The migratory fee amount was not confirmed from a readable official page.

It repeats the general advice that many countries want 6 months' passport validity, which is not confirmed as a UAE-specific rule for Australians here.

Longer stays or taking up work require an extension from the passport and registration authority in Yerevan before the 180 days end. Entry needs a valid passport, an ID card is not enough, the passport must be valid beyond the trip and a damaged passport is refused.

Immigration stamps an initial stay of up to 90 days on arrival, which can usually be extended once by a further 90 days, though there is no entitlement to it and it carries a fee (Auswaertiges Amt; Germany is also listed in Resolucion 5488 of 2022, Article 3 Literal A). The Auswaertiges Amt says travellers must complete the free online Check-Mig registration within 72 hours before entry (and again before departure) and show the confirmation to the airline before departing Germany. Passports must be valid for at least the intended stay; some travellers with 6 months or less beyond their departure date have been refused entry.

A residence permit must be applied for at a Public Service Hall in time for longer stays, and overstaying is a fineable offence. Passport must be valid until at least departure; an ID card is accepted by Georgia for EU citizens but the Foreign Office recommends a passport. You must complete the electronic entry declaration (IMUGA) within 96 hours before arrival. Passport: normally 6 months validity on arrival, but a temporary measure currently accepts 1 month (Maldives immigration also states 1 month); a national ID card is not accepted. An extension to 90 days must be applied for in the Maldives with a recommendation from your hotel/resort island. Overstaying 30 days without an approved extension can bring heavy fines and an entry ban.
fee_notes: Free for the 30-day visa on arrival; the IMUGA declaration is also free.

conditions_text: German citizens do not need a visa for tourism, transit or business (without employment) provided the stay is not longer than 180 days; the officer sets the days (1-180), extension possible but not guaranteed. The Auswaertiges Amt says air travellers no longer need a tourist card (FMM); land travellers need a paid FMM, which can be applied for online via INM, and must carry it on exit. Germany advises the passport be valid at least six months after arrival.
fee_notes: The Auswaertiges Amt says the land-entry tourist card (FMM) is fee-based but does not state the amount; air arrivals need no FMM. Peso amount not confirmed from a readable official page.

The border authorities decide the days granted, and the Auswärtiges Amt says the 90-day stay cannot be extended. Overstaying incurs a fine of 5 PEN per day. Passport must be valid at least six months on entry; ID cards are not accepted; you may occasionally be asked for onward or return tickets.

Passport, Personalausweis, temporary passport and child passport are accepted; a passport needs at least one blank page.

The passport must have at least 6 months' validity at entry. Provisional passports, ID cards and provisional ID cards are not accepted; the sex entry must be M or F. Working, even unpaid, is not allowed on this entry. Overstays risk fines and expulsion.

Singapore's MFA travel page says Singaporeans can enter Armenia visa-free for short stays of up to 180 days from the date of initial entry, counted within a 12-month period (Singapore government page; Armenia's own MFA pages could not be fetched). Rules can change at short notice.

Ensure the passport has space for entry and exit stamps and meets the minimum validity (confirm the exact figure with the Turkish Embassy).

Singapore MFA advice states Singapore passport holders can stay visa-free for up to 90 days in the UAE within a 180-day period, with no advance visa application. Passports bearing only a single name are refused entry under UAE federal rules. (The Singapore MFA page was too large for the fetch tool, so the 90/180-day wording and single-name rule come from a search-result excerpt of that page.)

The exemption covers tourism and business only (business means exploring commercial opportunities, meetings, signing contracts); it does not cover paid work. Armenia's current MFA list could not be opened when this was checked, so check mfa.am/en/whoneedvisa for any later change.

A yellow fever certificate is required if arriving from or recently transiting a risk country (children under 1 exempt). Extension to 90 days in total is applied for in the Maldives (per UK, German and Canadian government advice). The officer decides admissibility at the port.
fee_notes: Free; the IMUGA declaration is also free. No extension fee confirmed.

conditions_text: As of 5 February 2026 Brazilians may apply online for a Mexican electronic visa (visa electronica): single entry, air only, for stays of less than 180 days, no paid work, valid up to 180 days; apply at visaelectronica.sre.gob.mx, with an authorised e-visa carrying a QR code that should be printed or kept on a device. Brazilians in transit to a third country need a valid e-visa for each entry. Entering by land or sea, multiple entries, or a stay over 180 days requires a visa from a Mexican consulate (consular visa valid up to 180 days or up to 10 years). If the e-visa is denied you may apply for a consular visa. A valid US, Canadian, UK, Schengen or Japanese visa (or permanent residence there) replaces the visa; see the cascade rules.
fee_notes: The online process includes payment (embassy flyer). The e-visa fee and the consular visa fee were not stated on the official pages read, so no amount is given here.

conditions_text: Brazilian tourists do not need a visa (bilateral agreement B-3051). The Foreign Ministry table lists 90 days, extendable once for an equal period within 365 days from first entry; the Brazilian Embassy in Lima says the days are set by Peruvian immigration and shown in the TAM, and an extension must be requested from Migraciones before it expires. A passport valid six months (including for departure) is required; the RG identity card is accepted only when arriving on flights from Mercosur and associated states.

Brazilian nationals may enter the Philippines visa-free for 59 days from entry under a bilateral agreement (the DFA list gives 59 days to Brazil and Israel versus 30 for most others), provided they hold a return or onward ticket to their port of origin or next destination. The DFA list marks Brazil among nationals admissible with under 6 months' passport validity, but carry 6 months to avoid being refused boarding. Pre-arrival eTravel registration (etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app, free, within 72 hours before arrival, per the official eTravel FAQ and UK FCDO) is required for all arriving foreign passengers; airlines may ask for the QR code at check-in.
No visa required for ordinary passports for visits of up to 90 days in a 6-month period starting from the date of first entry (Serbian Ministry of Foreign Affairs).

Sri Lanka requires every foreign visitor, including Brazilians, to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online at eta.gov.lk before arrival. Brazil is not among the 40 nationalities eligible for the free tourist ETA (from 25 May 2026), so the standard paid tourist ETA applies, valid 30 days. Children under 12 of any nationality get a free tourist ETA for up to 30 days. Stays over 30 days incur extension fees, arranged via the Immigration e-services portal after arrival in Sri Lanka.
fee_notes: Tourist ETA for 'All other countries' (Brazil is in neither the free list of 40 nor the reciprocal list; the cheaper 'South Asian countries' column does not apply): US$50 if submitted by the applicant or at a Sri Lankan mission, US$60 on arrival. Children under 12 of any nationality get a free tourist ETA for up to 30 days. Per the official fee table at eta.gov.lk, read 2026-10-18.

conditions_text: Under a bilateral agreement, Brazilians do not need a visa for tourist trips to Türkiye, for a maximum stay of up to 90 days. Neither Turkey's foreign ministry nor Brazil's Itamaraty states a 180-day window for Brazilians, so do not assume one. Itamaraty (page updated April 2025) cites passport expiry at least 60 days after the exemption period ends, which is about 150 days for a full 90-day stay; confirm validity with the Turkish Embassy in Brasilia or the Consulate General in Sao Paulo.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists Brazil as 'Visa Free'. Under the bilateral visa-exemption agreement (UAE announcement: effective 2 June 2018), Brazilian ordinary-passport holders may stay up to 90 days in each 12-month period for tourism, transit or business, counted from first entry. Per the Brazilian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Abu Dhabi embassy alert, last updated 22 September 2022), the passport must be valid at least 6 months from the date of entry and emergency passports are not accepted. The exemption does not cover paid work, employment, study, research, internships or similar activities, and does not guarantee entry.

India is not on Japan's visa-exemption list (MOFA lists 74 exempt countries and regions, and India is not one), so Indian ordinary passport holders need a visa before travel. For tourism they can use the JAPAN eVISA: a single-entry short-term stay visa of up to 90 days, applied for through the Japan Visa Application Centres run by VFS Global in India, issued in electronic form instead of a passport sticker (eVISA started in India on 1 April 2024). At the airport you must show the 'visa issuance notice' on a mobile device with internet access; a PDF, photo, screenshot or printed copy is not accepted. Only ordinary passport holders can use the eVISA website, and you may be asked to attend an interview in person. Applications are accepted from 3 months before the travel date. For any other purpose, or a stay over 90 days, you apply at the Embassy or consulate (through VFS) and get a visa sticker in your passport.
fee_notes: From 1 July 2026 the Embassy of Japan in India lists a visa fee of 500 INR for Indian nationals (single or multiple); the VFS service fee is charged in addition.

conditions_text: US passport holders do not need a visa for short-term stays (tourism, business, visiting friends or relatives, with no paid work) under Japan's visa exemption arrangement. Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the United States among the countries covered, with a period of stay of 90 days granted on landing.

British citizens do not need to apply for a visa in advance for tourism or business visits of up to 90 days; permission to stay is granted on arrival (FCDO's wording is that you can get a visa on arrival for up to 90 days, and you must ask the immigration officer if you want multiple entries). Your passport must be valid for the length of your stay (no extra months required) and have a blank page for the entry stamp. A stay can be extended by applying at an immigration office in Japan; overstaying risks arrest, detention and a heavy fine. Paid work is not allowed on this status. FCDO lists no pre-travel authorisation for UK citizens today.

Canadian citizens do not need a visa for tourism for stays of up to 90 days; overstaying the 90-day visa-free limit is a criminal offence, and you cannot apply for a business, work or student visa after entering as a tourist. Global Affairs Canada says your passport must be valid for the expected duration of your stay (no six-month rule from Japan, though airlines may apply stricter rules). Customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket, and visitors are photographed and fingerprinted on arrival. No pre-travel authorisation is listed for Canadians today.

Australian passport holders do not need a visa for short stays of up to 90 days (tourism, a business trip or conference, or visiting friends and family). Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists Australia as visa-exempt with a 90 day period of stay. Smartraveller adds that you will be photographed and fingerprinted electronically on arrival (children under 16 are exempt), and that after entering under the visa exemption your status cannot be changed to a work, study or spouse visa without leaving and re-entering Japan with the right visa. Paid work is not allowed.

German citizens can enter Japan visa-free for short stays of up to 90 days. Auswaertiges Amt says travel documents must be valid for the intended length of stay; a passport or temporary passport is accepted, a Personalausweis is not. Stays of more than 180 days, and stays for work, study or vocational training, need a visa obtained before entry. Some airlines refuse boarding without a return or onward ticket within 90 days or a visa; the Auswaertiges Amt notes this is not the legal position, so check with your airline. Visit Japan Web pre-registration is no longer required but can speed up entry. No pre-travel authorisation is listed for Germans today.

Singapore passport holders do not need a visa for short-term entry into Japan. Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists Singapore among the visa-exempt countries, with a 90 day period of stay granted on landing; Singapore's MFA describes this as short-term entry of less than 90 days. Stays for work or longer than 90 days need the right visa or status arranged beforehand.

Brazilian nationals holding a valid ordinary (common) passport that meets the ICAO IC (electronic chip) standard can enter Japan without a visa for up to 90 consecutive days. Ordinary passports without a chip still need a visa obtained in advance. The exemption does not cover anyone entering to seek employment or to practise a profession or other occupation (including paid entertainment and sport). Under the exchange of diplomatic notes dated 24 July 2026 the measures run from 30 September 2026 to 29 September 2029 inclusive, extendable by notification; Japan can temporarily suspend them for public order, security or health reasons, or end them with at least 30 days' written notice.

Thailand's revised visa-exemption scheme took effect on 15 September 2026 (Ministry of Interior announcements published in the Royal Gazette on 31 August 2026). It replaced the earlier 60-day exemption with a 30-day exemption for tourism only; India is on the official list of 60 countries and territories granted the 30-day exemption. Indian ordinary-passport holders need a passport with at least six months' validity from the date of arrival. For land-border entries the 30-day exemption generally allows no more than two entries per calendar year. All foreign travellers must also complete Thailand's Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online before arrival, within the 3 days (72 hours) before they arrive.
fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-exempt entry. The TDAC is free of charge on the official Immigration Bureau portal (tdac.immigration.go.th); fake sites charge fees. Extending a stay by up to 30 days at a Thai immigration office is at the officer's discretion; the extension fee was not confirmed.

You can enter and leave only through the approved air, land and sea border gates (13 airports, 16 land and 13 sea gates) - the e-visa works only at the entry/exit points you select. Passport needs at least 6 months' validity.

Paid online through the portal's payment gateway; not refunded if the application is refused. Beware look-alike sites that add service fees.

Some visa-on-arrival access for Indians holding a used US, UK or Schengen visa is reported by agencies, but no official Egyptian or Indian government page confirming the conditions could be read, so do not plan around it. Agencies also report that an Egyptian travel agent's Letter of Guarantee may be asked for; this is not stated on the public portal pages, so check at application.
fee_notes: The portal's FAQ page lists a single-entry tourism e-visa at $25 and multiple-entry at $60, paid by card online; press reports from April 2026 say the portal now charges $30 and $65. Confirm the price on visa2egypt.gov.eg before paying. The 30-day stay is the standard tourist visa length given by Canada's and the UK's advice; the portal pages read did not state it.

The US State Department pages could not be opened (403), so US-specific advice was not read directly.

Passport must be valid at least 6 months after arrival and have at least one blank page.

FCDO does not give the e-visa price; the portal's FAQ page lists $25 single entry, though press reports from April 2026 say $30.

Arrival visas must be paid in cash, US dollars only. At the Taba land border a 14-day visa-free entry stamp is available if staying within the Sinai Peninsula. Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave Egypt. Overstaying the 30-day period can mean a fine on departure.

The e-visa fee is paid online; the portal FAQ lists $25 single entry, though press reports from April 2026 say $30.

conditions_text: Indian citizens need a visa and are in Category A of Morocco's e-visa scheme, so they can apply online at acces-maroc.ma with an ordinary passport valid for at least 90 days from the date of the application; no US/UK/Schengen visa or residence permit is needed for this route (India has been eligible since 10 January 2023). The e-visa is for tourism or business, is valid for a maximum of 180 days from issue, is for a single entry and a stay of no more than 30 days, and stays from several e-visas cannot be added together. Processing is 24 hours (express) or 72 hours (standard), counted in Moroccan working days. An e-visa does not guarantee entry: at the border you may be asked for a return ticket, proof of means (an international bank card or cash equivalent to more than 70 euros per person per day) and hospital/repatriation insurance for the stay.
fee_notes: Fee is charged on the acces-maroc.ma portal at payment and is non-refundable once the application is validated and paid; the amount was not stated on any official page that could be opened, so it is not given here (secondary reports quote 770 MAD standard / 1,100 MAD express - check the portal). The Indian embassy page says the e-visa can be extended up to six months with multiple entries, but the official conditions say single entry and 30 days; do not rely on an extension.

conditions_text: Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular portal lists the United States of America among the countries whose citizens are exempt from an entry visa, and the Moroccan National Tourist Office states that for all nationalities the maximum duration of a tourist trip is 90 days, with an extension requestable at the nearest police station for a further 90 days. The Tourist Office says a valid passport must cover at least the duration of the stay. The US State Department page (reported elsewhere to ask for six months' validity and a blank page) could not be opened, so the six-month figure is not confirmed from an official page read for this rule; six months is the safer margin. No onward-ticket or accommodation requirement is stated on the pages read. Entry conditions can change at short notice.

UK FCDO says the passport must have an expiry date at least 3 months after the date of arrival (other governments, and some airlines, quote six months, so six months is the safer margin), and that entry has been denied to some travellers with damaged passports. FCDO lists no traveller or arrival form; foreign currency of 100,000 MAD or more must be declared on entry or exit. Rule read from the UK FCDO page because Moroccan government pages block automated access.

The page lists no entry or exit form. Rule read from Global Affairs Canada because Moroccan government pages block automated access.

Australian citizens are on Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of countries whose citizens are exempt from an entry visa. Smartraveller says Australians generally do not need a visa to visit Morocco for less than 90 days, and the Moroccan National Tourist Office says the maximum duration of a tourist trip is 90 days for all nationalities (extension possible at a police station). Smartraveller says to contact a Moroccan embassy because entry conditions can change at short notice; its general note that many countries want 6 months' passport validity is not a Morocco-specific rule, and the Tourist Office only says the passport must cover the stay, so six months is the safer margin. Get the passport stamped on entry, as Smartraveller reports tourists having trouble leaving without one.

German citizens need no visa for tourist or business stays of up to 90 days (this is not EU freedom of movement; Morocco is outside the EU). Entry requires a passport, provisional passport or children's passport; a Personalausweis (identity card) is not accepted, and travellers refused on this basis must take the next flight back. The travel document must be valid for at least six months on arrival (Auswaertiges Amt), and entry is refused for a damaged passport or an incomplete machine-readable zone. Overstaying breaches Moroccan residence law and is prosecuted; extensions are decided by the foreigners' police and must be filed before the 90 days end. The page lists no entry form; foreign currency of 100,000 MAD equivalent or more must be declared.

Singapore MFA states Singaporeans can visit Morocco for up to 90 days without a visa, and Singapore is on Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of countries whose citizens are exempt from an entry visa. Singapore MFA's page was last modified 30 July 2026 and says entry requirements can change at short notice. It does not state a passport-validity or blank-page rule; the Moroccan National Tourist Office only says a valid passport must cover the duration of the stay, so six months' validity is the safer margin.

Brazilian citizens do not need a visa to enter and stay in Morocco for up to 90 days. The Brazilian Embassy in Rabat states the passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival in Morocco. The embassy also reports Brazilians travelling from Europe being stopped from boarding their return flight because of an irregular or undefined immigration status in Europe, so check your own status before travelling. Rule read from the Brazilian Embassy in Rabat page, not a Moroccan government page.

A France-Visas notice also says holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by a Schengen state do not need a short-stay visa. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (the official ETIAS website says it is not in operation).

conditions_text: No visa is needed for a visit, but a USA passport holder must hold an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before travelling to the UK. The ETA is in force today: the Immigration Rules ETA national list requires it for USA nationals travelling on or after 8 January 2025. GOV.UK says an ETA lets you travel to the UK, Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man for up to 6 months, and the Immigration Rules say it lasts two years from grant (or until the passport used in the application expires, if sooner) and allows multiple journeys, each visit capped at six months. It is tied to the passport used to apply, so a new passport needs a new ETA. Each traveller needs one, including babies and children. An ETA does not guarantee entry. Apply only through GOV.UK or the official UK ETA app; other websites charge extra.
fee_notes: ETA fee is 20 GBP per person (GOV.UK, ETA page, checked 2026-10-17); other sites may charge more.

IRCC: 'You don't need a visa or an eTA to travel to Canada' if you are a US national (US lawful permanent residents are also exempt). A valid US passport is recommended and is needed to fly; US citizens arriving by land or sea must carry proper identification showing citizenship. You must still meet Canada's basic entry requirements at the border. The permitted length of stay is not stated on the IRCC pages checked, so max stay is left blank.

British citizens (the UK passport categories IRCC lists, e.g. British citizen) are visa-exempt for Canada but need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) to fly to or transit through a Canadian airport. The eTA is in force today (IRCC: 'You need an eTA and a valid passport to board your flight to Canada'). It is tied to your passport and, per IRCC, valid for up to five years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first; a new passport needs a new eTA. You do NOT need an eTA when arriving by car, bus, train or boat (including a cruise ship), but you still need a valid passport. With a valid eTA you can make repeated short visits, normally for up to six months at a time; the officer at the border decides the length of each stay. Apply only on the official Canada.ca site. IRCC's list names UK passport categories rather than 'United Kingdom' as a single entry, so check that your passport category is on the eTA list.
fee_notes: eTA fee CAD $7 per person (non-refundable), paid when applying.

conditions_text: Home Affairs lists the ETA (subclass 601) and the eVisitor (subclass 651) by eligible passport, and this passport is on neither list, so a Visitor visa (subclass 600), tourist stream, must be applied for and granted before travel (use the tourist stream for applications from overseas). Home Affairs states the visa is for tourists, business visitors or visiting family, for up to 12 months; the length of stay is set case by case on the visa grant letter and may be less than requested, and it can be granted for single or multiple entry. You must show you are a genuine visitor intending to stay temporarily, and that you have, or have access to, enough money for your stay. Health and character requirements apply. Check processing times on the Home Affairs processing-time guide before booking non-refundable travel. No fixed number of days applies: Home Affairs states the stay as a period set on your grant.
fee_notes: Visa application charge: the Home Affairs page does not state a figure (it is shown by their Visa Pricing Estimator); not recorded here.

conditions_text: Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, subclass 601). Pre-travel online authorisation, in force today: the Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, subclass 601), applied for from outside Australia through the Australian ETA app (the Home Affairs page for the ETA was last updated 12 October 2026 and lists it as an open product). Home Affairs lists this passport as ETA-eligible. The ETA is valid for travel for 12 months or until the passport expires, whichever is shorter, with multiple entries; you can stay up to 3 months on each entry (entered here as 90 days). Tourism, visiting family or friends and some business visitor activities are allowed; you cannot work, and study or training is limited to 3 months in total. Catches from Home Affairs: you cannot apply with an Australian passport as a dual citizen; if you have a criminal conviction in any country, or have previously failed the health requirement, Home Affairs says to apply for a Visitor visa (subclass 600) instead; frequent or long stays may lead to questions about your travel purpose. Home Affairs suggests you do not make travel arrangements until the ETA is granted (most results are immediate, but not always).
fee_notes: Home Affairs: a service charge of AUD 20 applies to use the Australian ETA app, and there is no other charge payable for an ETA.

conditions_text: India is NOT on the DHA visa-exemption list (issued 09 December 2025): the list shows 90 days only for diplomatic, official and service passports, with the ordinary-passport column blank, so an ordinary Indian passport needs a visa or authorisation before travel. Two routes exist today. (1) ETA, in force now: South Africa's Electronic Travel Authorisation (official portal eta.dha.gov.za; launched officially 12 August 2026). India was one of the four original pilot nationalities (China, India, Indonesia, Mexico) named in the Minister's launch speech on gov.za, and the portal says holders of valid ordinary passports may apply online provided they will land at OR Tambo (Johannesburg), Cape Town, Lanseria or King Shaka airport. For visa-required travellers the ETA is issued as a port-of-entry visa (Section 10(a)); it is valid up to about 6 months, multiple entry, each stay up to 90 days, and the DHA says most outcomes arrive within 24 hours. The launch speech says the ETA will 'progressively become compulsory' for short stays from visa-required countries; no compulsory start date for India has been published, so treat it as the official online route and do not arrive without either an approved ETA or a visa. (2) Traditional visa: the South African High Commission in New Delhi states that all visa applications are lodged through VFS Global and that it does not accept applications directly; this route also covers arrival at any port other than the four ETA airports. Catches: the ETA FAQ says your passport must be valid for at least 7 months from your intended travel date, fees are non-refundable even if refused, an approved ETA does not guarantee entry, and a yellow-fever certificate is required if you arrive from a risk country. Carry return/onward ticket, accommodation and funds proof. Since 1 July 2026 all travellers must also complete the SARS online traveller declaration before entering or leaving.
fee_notes: The ETA fee amount is not stated on the DHA ETA pages checked; it is shown in the portal before you pay, and all ETA fees are non-refundable whether or not the application succeeds. VFS Global visa fees were not verified from an official page.

conditions_text: No visa needed: the Department of Home Affairs visa-exemption list (issued 09 December 2025, marked subject to change without notice) lists this nationality as exempt on ordinary passports for stays of up to 90 days, with no visa fee. Passport: the DHA says it must be valid for at least 30 days after the end of your intended visit and have at least one unused page for entry/departure endorsements; UK FCDO advises at least 2 blank pages, so carry 2. The Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) launched officially on 12 August 2026 at four airports (OR Tambo, Cape Town, Lanseria, King Shaka), but for visa-exempt travellers it is voluntary: the DHA ETA FAQ says visa-exempt travellers may travel without one and are processed under standard immigration procedures, so it is NOT required for this passport today. Catch: since 1 July 2026 every traveller entering or leaving South Africa must also complete the SARS online traveller declaration (a customs declaration, not a visa) before travelling. Carry a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of funds, as the immigration officer can ask for these at the port of entry. A yellow-fever certificate is needed if you arrive from a yellow-fever-risk country. Special requirements apply for travellers aged 17 and under; check the DHA.

India is not on Korea's list of K-ETA-exempt countries (the Korean mission list names Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macao, Canada, the US, Guam, 15 European countries and Australia and New Zealand) and Indian passport holders must obtain a Korean visa in advance through the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr): fill in the e-Form online, print it and submit it in person at the KVAC-VFS visa application centre (the Chennai embassy page says Indian nationals 'must apply for Korean Visa and obtain it through the Visa Portal'). For tourism the usual category is the short-term tourist visa (C-3-9) described on Korean embassy pages. K-ETA is for visa-free nationalities and is not the route for Indian passport holders. The length of stay is set on the visa issued, so no fixed number of days applies. Catch: Korea runs a separate visa-free scheme for Jeju Island for nationals of visa-required countries who fly directly to Jeju from overseas (not via Seoul or Busan); the Korean mission notice (April 2026) lists 23 excluded nationalities and India is not among them. The Indian Embassy in Seoul (advisory of 24 February 2026) says the Jeju facility is for short-term tourism only, does not cover mainland Korea and does not guarantee entry: immigration officers at Jeju airport decide, and it advises carrying printed return ticket, hotel booking for the full stay, itinerary, proof of funds and a passport valid at least six months. A trip that continues to Seoul or Busan needs the visa.

No visa needed for tourism or business of up to 90 days (stated in the US State Department's South Korea advisory; travel.state.gov blocked automated fetching, so that figure was read through a search result rather than an opened page). A K-ETA is normally required for visa-free entry, but US citizens are on the temporary K-ETA exemption list: the Korean consulate notice (Dallas, opened) says the exemption runs 1 January to 31 December 2026 (KST) and covers the US. The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

British citizens can enter for up to 90 days for short-term business or tourism without a visa (UK FCDO). FCDO says you must have an onward or return ticket and that your passport must have an expiry date after you leave Korea. A K-ETA is usually required for visa-free entry but British nationals are temporarily exempt until 31 December 2026 (FCDO and the Korean mission exemption list). The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

Canadians can visit for tourism or business for up to 180 days without a visa (Global Affairs Canada; a Korean foreign-ministry mission page seen in search also describes six months for Canadians). Canada is the longest visa-free period of the eight passports. A passport valid beyond the expected departure date is required (transport companies may apply stricter rules). A K-ETA is normally required for visa-free entry but Canadians are exempt until 31 December 2026 (Global Affairs Canada and the Korean mission exemption list). The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. German citizens (EU/Schengen nationals) can enter Korea without a visa for short stays that Germany's Auswaertiges Amt words as fewer than 90 days, with no employment. The passport must be valid on arrival with no minimum remaining validity required; a provisional passport is accepted but a Personalausweis (ID card) is not. A K-ETA is normally required but German citizens need none until 31 December 2026. The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Singapore passport holders do not need a visa for short-term entry; Singapore's MFA words this as under 90 days and the Korean embassy in Singapore describes the allowed stay as 90 days (both read through search results, not an opened page). The Korean embassy in Singapore states Singapore passport holders are exempt from K-ETA until 31 December 2026, and that there is no requirement on the passport's remaining validity as long as it stays valid throughout the stay in Korea. The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Brazilians do not need a visa for tourism, business, family visits or events of up to 90 days, but they must obtain a K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) before boarding, and it is in force today. Brazil is not on the K-ETA temporary exemption list (the list is Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macao, Canada, US, Guam, 15 European countries, Australia and New Zealand), so the requirement applies now. Brazil's foreign ministry (MRE) states the K-ETA is mandatory for stays of up to 90 days and that a visa is needed for stays of more than 90 days; the Korean embassy in Brazil says the K-ETA does not replace a visa, must be applied for at least 72 hours before travel on the official site k-eta.go.kr only (many look-alike sites charge more), and that a denied applicant cannot reapply successfully unless circumstances change significantly. The K-ETA guide on k-eta.go.kr states the fee is KRW 10,000 and processing is generally within 72 hours. The Korean embassy also says travellers who only visit Jeju on a direct flight do not need a K-ETA, but anyone planning to visit other regions needs one before entering Jeju.
fee_notes: K-ETA fee KRW 10,000 per the k-eta.go.kr guide; non-refundable per Korean mission notices.

Indian nationals normally need a Mexican visa (India is on INM's list of countries that require one), but the INM page lists a valid, unexpired visa from Canada as an accepted alternative to a Mexican visa, alongside proof of permanent residence there. With one of these documents you may enter as a tourist or business visitor without a Mexican visa, still with a valid passport. By air there is no paper form: the digital FMM (FMMd) is generated at immigration and the officer stamps your passport with the days granted. By land you must carry a completed FMM (it can be filled in online beforehand or at the border). Visitors may not stay more than 180 days; the officer sets the actual days. No paid work. Confirm with the nearest Mexican consulate that your specific visa qualifies before booking.
fee_notes: The migratory fee for tourist entry is set each year in the Ley Federal de Derechos (2026 rates from 1 January 2026); the peso amount was not confirmed from a readable official page. Check the INM 2026 fee table.

Indian passport holders with a valid UK visa or residence permit may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for 90 days in any 180-day period.
